clue.text: Conceal wife's criticism

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a rap is a rebuke or piece of criticism, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A husband hides the telling-off his wife gave him.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something up is to cover it so it cannot be seen, a synonym for hiding it.

clue.text: No progressive can break up any race riot

indicators.note: breaking up the words scatters them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a political disturbance can be broken up by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactionary opposes political or social change, the opposite of a progressive.

clue.text: A sequence of blows from him finished off the vermin

definitions.text: A sequence of blows from him finished off the vermin

parts.words: A sequence of blows from him finished off the vermin
parts.note: blows here are breaths into a pipe: the piper of Hamelin played a tune that led the rats away

explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale the piper of Hamelin lured the rats away by playing his pipe.

clue.text: Musical family ready to expend energy in performance

indicators.note: a performance puts things through their paces, so these letters are acted out in a new order
spending energy means using it up, so that letter is removed from the word ready

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A family of performers gets ready to put all their effort into a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expend' takes E out of READY, leaving RADY; 'in performance' then rearranges FAMILY plus RADY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the Lerner and Loewe stage show based on Shaw's Pygmalion.

clue.text: Awkward situation over killer in island

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot, an awkward situation
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A tricky moment with a murderer on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killer' looks like a murderer; it is the killer whale. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Buzzer being no longer connected to manual control, lose it

parts.note: a fly is an insect that buzzes
off means disconnected, as a power supply is switched off
the handle is the part you hold to control something by hand

explanation.surface: An insect breaks free of a hand-operated device and goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like an electric bell but is a fly. 'being' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for suddenly losing one's temper.

clue.text: One has to come down again to the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to reland is to land once more, coming down again from the air

explanation.surface: A traveller has to fly home to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to' (before 'the country') are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation, a particular country.

clue.text: Endless stream under a power shower expected now?

indicators.note: in a down clue the stream sits beneath the other pieces, so it comes last

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A forecast of a heavy downpour with a stream running beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'April showers', the rain expected in that month; 'Endless' cuts RILL to RIL.
explanation.definitionFit: This month is proverbially the time of showers, so a shower may be expected in it.

clue.text: You must take prisoner for hearing in remote territory

indicators.note: for hearing means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: you plus con, a convict or prisoner

explanation.surface: An order to capture someone in a faraway frontier land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must take' joins YOU and CON, the old lag; spoken together they give the Canadian territory's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a sparsely populated territory in north-western Canada.

clue.text: Biblical king's delight with church author

parts.note: King James gave his name to the Authorised Version of the Bible
joy is a synonym for delight
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A Bible-reading monarch takes pleasure in the church's company.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish novelist who wrote Ulysses and Finnegans Wake is a celebrated example of a writer.

clue.text: A thousand going on short plane journey

indicators.note: one piece is added on after the other, so the thousand comes at the end
short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree, the plane tree
K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: A thousand passengers take a quick flight somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft, but it is the plane tree, shortened to TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous trip, often on foot, so it is a kind of journey.

clue.text: In a daze, replaces men?

parts.note: read as re-places, i.e. puts back: the word puts written backwards
OR, other ranks, is the forces' term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone in a fog swaps out the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' is split as re-places, meaning 'puts back', so PUTS is written backwards as STUP; 'In a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, much the same as a daze.

clue.text: One with a tale to tell, to be honest, not entirely popular

definitions.text: One with a tale to tell

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: frankly means to be honest, speaking candidly
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A storyteller, if we are frank, is not universally liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, where one of the pilgrims, a landowner, tells his own story.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Canterbury Tales the Franklin, a country landowner, is one of the pilgrims who tells a story.

clue.text: How ruthlessly snakes operate?

parts.note: the idiom for doing something without mercy is also literally true of cold-blooded reptiles

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without pity or deliberately, and snakes are literally cold-blooded creatures.

clue.text: First course perhaps like this at university

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
to be up is to be in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A remark about starting a degree course on the right lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First course' reads as a university's first-year course, but it is the starter of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is a typical starter, the dish served first in a meal, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: As car was working, I skipped school

parts.note: auto is a short word for automobile, a car
did act means performed or operated, i.e. was working

explanation.surface: Someone explains they went truant while their car was running.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: someone self-taught can say they skipped school. 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who teaches themselves never needed formal education, so they could say they missed out school.

clue.text: Handyman who holds forth at Christmas?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an orator is someone who holds forth, making speeches

explanation.surface: An odd-job man who lectures everyone over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hanging festive decorations, but Christmas is just the month. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and paperhanger is a tradesman of the handyman sort.

clue.text: Insect seen barely to move on hot wind

indicators.note: one piece comes on after the others, so the run naked part goes last

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
air is a moving current of air, a breeze or wind
to streak is to run naked, moving with nothing on

explanation.surface: A bug spotted drifting along on a warm breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means naked, not scarcely: to move naked is to streak. 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstreak is a small butterfly with fine streaks on its wings, a kind of insect.

clue.text: In agony, raced to suppress rising depression

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down inside, so one word is enclosed by the other

parts.note: tore means rushed or raced

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a rut is a groove or hollow, a depression in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone in pain hurried along to put down a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'In' of 'In agony' is a link; 'rising' signals the upward reading of the depression, and 'to suppress' wraps the racing word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture means extreme suffering, much the same as agony.

clue.text: It takes mice to find a way right inside ship

indicators.note: inside means these letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: a keel is the spine of a ship, and by extension a ship itself
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A ship's cat is found holding the course to starboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon that preys on mice and voles.

clue.text: Some leg of veal?

definitions.meaning: part of the leg, the fleshy back of the shin below the knee
veal is the meat of a young bovine animal, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A butcher's query about a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the muscle at the back of the lower leg and the young cow that veal comes from.

clue.text: Mental disturbance is troubling this year

indicators.note: troubling suggests stirring things up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says the past twelve months have been hard on the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is a state of uncontrollable emotion, a recognised form of mental upset.

clue.text: Stupefy with cold in unfinished building

parts.note: a house is a building
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A half-built house is so chilly it stuns you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts HOUSE to HOUS. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hocus is an old term for drugging or stupefying someone.

clue.text: Holy man had us converted

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious figure won us over to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests a religious conversion, fitting the holy man, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic, a holy man.

clue.text: Light, extremely short dress

parts.note: a robe is a long loose garment, a dress

explanation.surface: A very short frock in a pale colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a description of the dress; it is the definition, a flashing lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp that gives rapid flashes, a kind of light.

clue.text: Fish -—- a final piece

parts.note: cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: A fish served as the last item.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing section of a piece of music or a concluding passage.

clue.text: Got beneath rose

parts.note: under is a synonym for beneath
stood means rose to one's feet

explanation.surface: Something was found underneath a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to grasp its meaning, a colloquial synonym for comprehending it.

clue.text: A corps caught in short spell of turbulence get proper food

indicators.note: the other pieces are trapped inside the shortened word
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a squall is a sudden violent gust of wind, a brief spell of turbulence

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught in a storm need a good meal.

clue.text: Cross when speaking, so appears this?

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in rood screen
